newsitem.title: INDIA: India party to review crucial ties with government.
newsitem.headline: India party to review crucial ties with government.

text.p: India's Congress party plans to review on Monday its backing of the minority United Front governmment and embattled former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's role as Congress parliamentary leader, officials said.
Senior leaders have called for the review of the party's support over the past five months to Prime Minister Deve Gowda, the officials said.

Congress politicians said a move was also afoot to ask former prime minister Rao at the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting on Monday to step down as head of the party in parliament following a string of criminal charges against him.
Rao gave up the party's presidency in September under pressure over the brewing criminal cases.
"The Congress does not want an early election, so we do not want to withdraw support to the (Deve Gowda) government," a senior Congress official told Reuters on Sunday.

"But there is a great demand to ensure that the government does not take our support for granted. The party will look at the merits of the demand to withdraw support to Deve Gowda," the official said.

Deve Gowda formed a minority United Front government in June with the support of Congress after inconclusive April/May general elections returned his group with just 115 seats in the 545-member lower house of parliament. Congress, despite its worst defeat in a general election, won 142 seats.

Simmering tensions between the two parties worsened last month when they backed rival leaders for the chief minister's job in the country's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, where local polls produced a hung assembly.

"Our position on Uttar Pradesh remains unchanged," a Congress spokesman said, refering to the party's backing to Mayawati (eds: one name), a woman leader of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) that represents the lowest Hindu castses.
Rao has been charged in two bribery and forgery scandals and also named in a 1983 case of cheating. A court will decide on Tuesday whether to extend Rao's premptive bail against arrest.
Rao's successor as Congress president, Sitaram Kesri, is under pressure to remove him from the Congress Parliamentary Party's leadership.
Kesri, a former cabinet colleague and friend of Rao, is grappling with the temptation that many influential Congress rebels would return if he fires Rao, Congress officials said.
Newspapers said one such breakaway faction was Finance Minister P. Chidmabaram's Tamil Maanila Congress, currently a key member of the United Front.

"Tamil Maanila Congress chief G.K. Moopanar is willing to return to the Congress if P.V. Narasimha Rao is removed from the post of Congress Party Parliament leader," the Asian Age said, quoting Congress sources.
The Hindu newspaper said Kesri had asked senior aides to start talks with other former Congress stalwarts, now Deve Gowda's allies, to woo them back to the party.
"The process of 'unity' has got an impetus because it is understood that Mrs Sonia Gandhi is also keen on such a development," the Hindu said.
The Italian-born widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was assassinated while seeking re-election, has so far resisted Congress pressure to take charge of the party.
But, the Hindu said: "The new party president, Mr Sitaram Kesri, has had a number of meetings with her."
